predecessors.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: the Upper March around Zaragoza: the page names only the city and its rulers

successors.name: Almoravid dynasty
successors.text: Zaragoza and what remained of the Hudid realm in May 1110

ledger.x: 1013: the Banu Tujib rule Zaragoza as an independent taifa after the fall of the Caliphate of Córdoba.
1039: the Banu Hud take Zaragoza from the Banu Tujib.

c. 1040: Lérida is given to a son and becomes a separate taifa. 'At some point prior to his death in 1046,' al-Musta'in gave Lérida to his younger son Yusuf (ruler 1039/1046–1078/1081); the Zaragoza page: 'Between c. 1040 and c. 1105, the Taifa of Lérida was separate from that of Zaragoza'. The page gives no boundary…
1078: al-Muqtadir and his brother Yusuf of Lérida go to war: 'he and his brother fought a civil war in 1078–81'.
1081: the civil war ends with al-Muqtadir's death 'in late 1081', when 'the ṭāʾifa was divided between his two sons'; Mundhir (Yusuf's nephew) holds Lérida from 1081.
1081: Tortosa passes to al-Mundhir at the division of the kingdom.
1081: Dénia passes to al-Mundhir's realm at the division of the kingdom.
1110 (May): the Almoravids take Zaragoza, 'the last independent Taifa kingdom'.

wars.name: Civil war between al-Muqtadir and Yusuf of Lérida
wars.outcome: Brothers of the Banu Hud fought for Lérida; al-Muqtadir died in late 1081 and the realm was divided between his sons.

wars.name: Hudid annexation of Tortosa and Dénia
wars.outcome: Zaragoza annexed Tortosa in 1060 (or 1061) and Dénia in 1076; both passed to Mundhir at the division of 1081.

wars.name: Aragonese advance on the Upper Ebro
wars.outcome: Aragon moved its capital to Huesca in 1096; 'In 1100, Peter, now king of Aragon, captured Barbastro' (Lérida page); in 1101 the capture of Pomar de Cinca and Albalate de Cinca 'brought the Aragonese up to Lérida itself'.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Zaragoza
wars.outcome: Zaragoza was taken in May 1110, ending the last independent taifa; Aragon conquered the city in 1118.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line or survey; the pages name cities and rulers, not boundaries.
